i1040sd p. 10, Example 1—Basis Reported to the IRS, read with a Form 1099-DA (box 1f proceeds $6,000, box 1g basis $2,000, box 2 checked, held 3 years, no adjustments): $6,000 on Schedule D line 8a column (d), $2,000 in column (e), $4,000 in column (h). Box J is the Form 8949 box such a sale would carry if listed (i8949 p. 4, Box D or Box J).
i1040sd p. 11, continuation of Example 1 (a second transaction with proceeds $5,000 and basis $3,000), Form 1099-DA branch: line 8a column (d) $11,000, column (e) $5,000, column (h) $6,000.

i1040sd p. 11, Example 2—Basis Not Reported to the IRS, Form 1099-DA branch (proceeds $6,000, basis $2,000, box 2 not checked): not on line 8a; reported on Form 8949. Column (e) is the correct basis, taken as the $2,000 shown; column (h) = $6,000 - $2,000 = $4,000 (i1040sd p. 11, column (h) Example 1). Box K (long-term) is synthetic: the example gives no holding period.

i1040sd p. 11, Example 3—Adjustment, Form 1099-DA branch (proceeds $6,000, reported basis $2,000, box 2 checked, basis incorrect) with column (h) Example 3 (column (g) ($1,000), column (h) $3,000). Code B and a correct basis of $3,000 are the scaffolding that gives the stated ($1,000) (i8949 p. 11, Worksheet for Basis Adjustments: line 1 $2,000, line 2 $3,000, line 3 ($1,000)). Box J (long-term) is synthetic.

Schedule D line 1b totals Form 8949 rows with box A or box G (f1040sd p. 1, "Box A or Box G checked"), so a box A sale and a box G sale add: (d) 500,000 + 300,000 = 800,000; (e) 400,000 + 350,000 = 750,000; (h) 100,000 - 50,000 = 50,000. Predicted by hand before running.

A box H sale (basis not reported to the IRS) cannot go on line 1a: i1040sd p. 10, Lines 1a and 8a, "shows basis was reported to the IRS". Gate sales[a].bad_aggregate; refusal text as sales.refuse.aggregate.basis records it.
